intro: The India e-Arrival card is a free online form that foreign visitors and OCI cardholders can fill in within 72 hours before arriving. It’s arrival information, not a visa, so you still need your e-Visa or visa.
cardText: India’s free online arrival card: who fills it in, when, and how.

sections.heading: What is the India e-Arrival card?
sections.text: It’s the online version of the landing card you used to fill in on the plane. It collects your arrival details for India’s immigration authorities. It doesn’t replace a visa.

sections.heading: When and where to fill it in
sections.text: Complete it within 72 hours before you arrive, on the Bureau of Immigration website (boi.gov.in), on indianvisaonline.gov.in, or in the official “Indian Visa Su-Swagatam” mobile app. It’s free.

sections.heading: Watch out for fake e-Arrival card websites
sections.text: Some websites charge fees for the e-Arrival card. The official service is free. You don’t need to pay anyone, including us, to fill it in.

sections.heading: Do I still need a visa?
sections.text: Yes. You still need your e-Visa or regular visa. The e-Arrival card is extra information, not permission to enter.

sections.heading: What the India e-Arrival card asks for
sections.text: Your passport details, your flight or travel details, your address in India and your contact details. Have your passport and visa to hand. Fill in a separate India e-Arrival card for each traveller, including children.

faqs.q: Is the India e-Arrival card free?
faqs.a: Yes. The official e-Arrival card is free.

faqs.q: When should I fill in the e-Arrival card?
faqs.a: Within 72 hours before you arrive in India.

faqs.q: Is the e-Arrival card a visa?
faqs.a: No. It’s arrival information. You still need a valid visa or e-Visa.

title: India e-Arrival Card 2026: Who Needs It and How
